title: EU GDPR readiness checklist
legal_review_status: Plain-language aid prepared from the regulation text and EDPB guidance for small organisations. Not reviewed by counsel and not legal advice. Have a qualified professional confirm applicability and wording before relying on any item as an obligation for your organisation.
effective_status_note: The GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679) is in force. Small size does not remove its application; whether it applies to you depends on your processing and the people it concerns.

sources.label: EDPB: data protection guide for small businesses

controls.title: Lawful basis for each purpose
controls.question: Which of the six lawful bases applies to each way you use personal data for this system?
controls.requirement: Each processing purpose has one documented lawful basis. Consent is only one of them.
controls.guidance: Do not default to consent. Pick the basis that actually fits.

controls.title: Special-category data
controls.question: Does the system process data revealing race, health, religion, biometrics or other special categories, including group attributes used for fairness testing?
controls.requirement: Special-category data needs an additional condition under Art. 9 as well as an Art. 6 basis.
required_evidence: Justification for holding group attributes for testing
controls.guidance: Fairness testing often needs sensitive attributes. Record why and how they are protected.

controls.title: Transparency to individuals
controls.question: Are individuals told who you are, why you process their data, and their rights?
controls.requirement: Privacy information is concise, clear and given at the right time.
controls.guidance: Include meaningful information about the logic of automated decisions where Art. 22 applies.

controls.title: Automated individual decisions
controls.question: Does the system make decisions with legal or similarly significant effects on people, solely by automated means?
controls.requirement: Such decisions are allowed only in limited cases and need safeguards including human review, a way to express a view and to contest the decision.
required_evidence: Evidence reviewers can and do change outcomes
controls.guidance: An explanation chart alone does not meet this item.
controls.not_applicable_reason: The system was not marked as making or driving decisions about people.

controls.title: Purpose limitation and data minimisation
controls.question: Is every personal field used here adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary?
controls.requirement: Data is collected for specified purposes and limited to what is necessary.
required_evidence: Data inventory with purpose for each personal field
Review of model inputs against it
controls.guidance: The automatic privacy scan lists candidate personal-data columns to start from.

controls.title: Accuracy
controls.question: Are there checks that the data behind decisions is accurate and kept up to date?
controls.requirement: Inaccurate personal data is corrected or erased without delay.
controls.guidance: Drift and missing-data results can support this item.

controls.title: Data protection by design and by default
controls.question: Were privacy measures built into the system design, such as pseudonymisation and limited access?
controls.requirement: Appropriate measures are built in from design, and by default only necessary data is processed.
controls.guidance: Short written design notes are better evidence than none.

controls.title: Processors and contracts
controls.question: Do vendors process personal data on your behalf?
controls.requirement: A written contract with required terms governs each processor.
controls.guidance: Include cloud, analytics and annotation vendors.

controls.title: Records of processing
controls.question: Do you keep a record of your processing activities?
controls.requirement: Records are kept. The small-organisation exemption is narrow and does not apply to processing that is regular or likely to risk individuals.
controls.guidance: A simple spreadsheet is accepted if it has the required fields.

controls.title: Security of processing
controls.question: What technical and organisational measures protect confidentiality, integrity and availability?
controls.requirement: Measures are appropriate to the risk and tested or reviewed regularly.
controls.guidance: This tool cannot verify your infrastructure. A reviewer judges the evidence.

controls.title: Personal data breach notification
controls.question: Can you detect a breach and notify the supervisory authority within the required period and affected people where needed?
controls.requirement: A procedure exists to assess, record and notify breaches.
controls.guidance: Check the current notification period in Art. 33.

controls.title: Data protection impact assessment
controls.question: Is the processing likely to result in a high risk to individuals, for example systematic evaluation of people by automated means?
controls.requirement: A DPIA is carried out before high-risk processing starts.
required_evidence: DPIA, or a recorded reason none is required
controls.guidance: Automated profiling that affects people is a common trigger.

controls.title: Rights of individuals
controls.question: Can people access, correct, erase, restrict or object to the processing of their data, and who handles requests?
controls.requirement: Requests are handled within the required period without undue cost.
controls.guidance: Test the procedure with a sample request.

controls.title: Transfers outside the EEA
controls.question: Is personal data transferred outside the European Economic Area, including to vendors or staff in other countries?
controls.requirement: A valid transfer mechanism applies to each transfer.
required_evidence: Transfer list with mechanism for each
controls.guidance: Hosting and support tools are common hidden transfers.
